There are characters aplenty within Formula One, a sport that attracts the larger‑than-life, and at the sharp end it can be a parade ground for swaggering egos. Yet the newest addition to the paddock is a man whose quietly spoken, understated thoughtfulness and insight are compelling. Now part of the Mercedes team, Reid Wiseman has been to the moon and with it brings a perspective like no other.

Wiseman was one of four astronauts, alongside Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen, who completed the Artemis II lunar flyby in April. Last month Wiseman, the mission’s commander, became an ambassador for Mercedes’ F1 team, formalising a relationship that had been growing over several years, to the delight of his daughter, Katey, a fan of the newly crowned world champion, Kimi Antonelli.

The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.

Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.

items.title: The Spin | Sandpapergate’s ‘war of the ghosts’ highlights perils of relying on recall
items.summary:
One of Pat Cummins or Usman Khawaja must be lying about Cape Town? Not so, says a professor of memory

In 1932, the English psychologist Frederic Bartlett used cricket as a metaphor for memory. “When I make the stroke I do not, as a matter of fact, produce something absolutely new and I never merely repeat something old” he wrote in his landmark book Remembering: a Study in Experimental and Social Psychology.

Bartlett posited that remembering the past is just like playing a stroke, a cover drive say, in cricket. You can never repeat the stroke exactly, so like a fingerprint or snowflake, no two cover drives are exactly the same, even when played by the same person. Each cover drive is “manufactured” afresh in the new circumstances, the “schemata of the moment and their interrelations”.

The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.

Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager.   • Peru win makes her first Indigenous Australian world champion in open category

With the surfing world her oyster, Leihani Zoric has set her sights stratospherically high after the 14-year-old stunned a star-studded field to be crowned the youngest ever ISA Open World Surfing Champion and claim a second world title this year.

Zoric, who was still 13 when she won the ISA under-18 world title in September, added a gold medal to her burgeoning individual palmarès with victory in Peru over the weekend, when she emerged triumphant ahead of established stars of the surfing world such as Stephanie Gilmore, Tyler Wright, Carissa Moore and Johanne Defay.

items.title: Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares faces deportation after ICE arrest
items.summary:
• Venezuelan boxer, 41, held at El Paso facility

  • Lawyers say three-weight champion is in US legally

  • ICE alleges Linares overstayed authorized visit

Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares has been detained by US immigration authorities in Texas, despite his lawyers insisting the retired Venezuelan fighter is legally in the country.

Linares is being held at the El Paso Processing Center, according to federal detention records reviewed by the San Antonio Express-News. US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said he was arrested at El Paso International Airport on Sunday after overstaying the period he was authorized to remain in the country.

Ben Earl has called on Nations Championship organisers to introduce a destination finals weekend, with Las Vegas, Hong Kong and Brazil among the England back-row’s suggestions.

Twickenham will host the inaugural finals weekend this month and while Qatar was due to stage the second edition in 2028, it recently pulled out due to the conflict in the Middle East. Qatar’s plan to host in 2032 looks unlikely and a tournament sponsorship deal with Qatar Airways valued at £80m has also fallen through.

items.title: Rassie Erasmus’s tired ref-blaming act is wearing thin – South Africa deserve better | Robert Kitson
items.summary:
Springboks’ achievements are remarkable but their head coach lacks statesmanship, diplomacy and good grace in defeat

So here we go again. Exactly five years have passed since South Africa’s head coach, Rassie Erasmus, first felt the full force of World Rugby’s ire for criticising match officials. And guess what? This most habitual of offenders has just copped another lengthy ban – and deservedly so – for his latest intemperate comments, notable as ever for their total lack of statesmanship, diplomacy or good grace in defeat.

To his acolytes his outspoken nature is part of what makes Rassie such a groot leier (great leader). To many others it simply cements his status as a serial prat. For the avoidance of any doubt everyone respects the remarkable achievements both of Erasmus and his double World Cup-winning teams. It is the rest of the package, sadly, that is too often a major letdown.

items.title: Bryson DeChambeau adds star quality to DP World Tour after demise of LIV Golf
items.summary:
• Player in ‘category one’ status after US Open win

  • Golfer ineligible for PGA Tour due to blanket ban

Bryson DeChambeau will add star quality to the DP World Tour next season after it was confirmed the two-time major winner has joined the circuit after the demise of LIV Golf. The American heads a list of high-profile names who will perform regularly in Europe in 2027 following LIV’s bankruptcy.

Intrigue had surrounded DeChambeau’s future. As a poster boy for LIV and its Saudi Arabian-backed disruption scheme, he appeared unwilling to feature again on traditional tours. Yet it became increasingly clear what limited options he had. The PGA Tour has been unwilling to offer an easy pathway for the 33-year-old, who in theory can now play his way back there via the DP World Tour. Cards will be available on the PGA Tour for 2028 through DP World Tour rankings. DeChambeau has become increasingly keen on content creation, which fuelled speculation he may skip mainstream competition entirely.

Continue reading...
items.t: Bryson DeChambeau adds star quality to DP World Tour after demise of LIV Golf
